question: Does an in-graph Gram tap, which adds zero graph dispatches, perturb the backbone step?

method.entry_point: traced-module _forward, identical inputs, host wall clock
method.note: baseline re-measured with the same clock; the profile's 266.4 ms is device execution time and is not comparable

mechanism.evidence: returned Gram row components are equal (402300.375, 402300.375), i.e. <anchor,c> == <c,c> under a repeated identical input, so the resident anchor holds the previous invocation's output

pre_compilation_estimate.why_wrong: the proxy priced arithmetic only; the measured cost is dominated by fp32 materialisation, the 1 MB alias write-back, and the fact that a tail-appended reduction has nothing left to overlap with

runtime_contracts_learned: a tensor returned both plainly and as an alias target is deduplicated by XLA, leaving the alias index dangling
an aliased output is written in place and does not return to host, so aliases must occupy the tail of the output tuple
shared_weights.store_key carried no graph discriminator, so a structurally different graph silently received the baseline backbone's shards
the builder traces one SPMD program for all ranks, so rank-dependent behaviour must read device state rather than a Python-time rank lookup
next: re-base the three surviving second-round candidates (pre-certified lattice, deficit ledger downshift, idle-lane ground truth) on a host-side Gram row

cost_decomposition.reductions_note: noalias is identical to post minus the write-back and lands below baseline, i.e. the two full-length reductions hide inside the existing overlap schedule
cost_decomposition.writeback_evidence: halving the write-back from 1 MB (fp32) to 512 KB (bf16) changed nothing: 269.66 vs 269.94 ms
cost_decomposition.interpretation: the cost is the cross-invocation in-place write contract itself, not bandwidth

host_alternative.extra_data_movement: none; the host already holds every anchor because the backbone returns its output each real step

verdict: do not build the in-graph tap; compute the Gram row on the host
law_refinement: fusing into an existing invocation is free only while it needs no cross-invocation resident state; requiring an alias costs a fixed, size-independent penalty
